clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the au­
thority vested in me by sections 10 and 12  
of the Pay Readjustment Act of 1942, as  
amended (56 Stat. 363, 364, 60 Stat. 858;  
37 U. S. C. 110,112), and sections 208 (c)  
and 305 (a) of the National Security Act  
of 1947 (61 Stat. 504, 508; 5 U. S. C. 626 c_  
and 171 l), Executive Order No. 9871 of  
July 8, 1947, as amended by Executive  
Order No. 9976 of July 12,1948, prescrib­
ing regulations governing the granting of  
allowances for quarters and subsistence  
to enlisted men of the Army, Air Force,  
Navy, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard,  
and per diem allowances to members of  
such services and Coast and Geodetic  
Survey and Public Health Service on duty  
outside the continental United States  
or in Alaska, is hereby amended and ex­
tended as follows:

1. Part ID  of the said order is amend­
ed to read as follows:
“D. Men traveling on duty, including  
detentioris not exceeding thirty-one days  
at any one place, when not furnished  
sleeping-car or stateroom accommoda­
tions or other quarters and rations in  
kind, shall be granted a daily allowance  
of $5.00 :  Provided,  that when quarters  
in kind are furnished, they shall be en­
titled only to an allowance for subsist­
ence at the rates prescribed below :

1. Meals required to be taken in dining Rate  
car on train or in dining room per
on steamer: meal
Morning meal ____________________$l. 25
Noon meal_______________ ________ 1 .50
Evening meal ___________________ 1. 75

2. Meals taken elsewhere:
Morning meal __________l________ 1.00
Noon meal _________ _____________ 1.25
Evening meal _________________1. 50
And provided further,  that when quar­
ters are not furnished for the day of such  
travel, the allowance for quarters shall  
be $3.00, except that when the allowance  
for meals on any one day is in excess of  
$2.00, the allowance for quarters shall be  
reduced by the amount of such excess.”

2. This order shall become effective on  
June 1, 1949, and the said Executive  
Order No. 9871, as amended by Executive 
Order No. 99761 of July 12, 1948 and this  
order, shall continue in effect during the  
fiscal year ending June 30, 1950, unless  
sooner modified or revoked;

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 10061 (14 FR 2915 (Federal Register of June 3, 1949)) was signed June 2, 1949. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. It amends Executive Order No. 9871 of July 8, 1947 (as already amended by Executive Order No. 9976 of July 12, 1948) on allowances to enlisted men: item 1 restates Part D of the said order (a daily allowance for men traveling on duty, with meal rates), and item 2 makes the order effective June 1, 1949 and provides that the amended Executive Order No. 9871 and this order “shall continue in effect during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950, unless sooner modified or revoked”. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated by that own-terms sunset, the end of the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950. The wording “unless sooner modified or revoked” requires a search for an earlier modification or revocation. The held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 9871, run with and without a trailing footnote digit, found only Executive Order No. 9976 (the earlier amendment), the Federal Register page that also holds Executive Order 10060, Executive Order 10061 itself and the American Presidency Project copies; no later order modifies or revokes Executive Order No. 9871 or this order. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists one hit for this order, which is a cross-reference attached to Executive Order No. 9976 that points to this order, not a later event. The U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. The dossier splits the order into five fragments (two of them mere continuations of the meal-rate table); the inventory is corrected to the three operative pieces: the amending lead, the restated Part D, and the effective-date and duration item.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order's own sunset is the first end: no held text modifies or revokes Executive Order No. 9871 or this order before June 30, 1950. The end date recorded is June 30, 1950 on the inclusive reading, because the order continues “during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950”; the exclusive reading, under which it stops when June 30 begins, is disclosed as the alternative. Amendments of Part D by a later order would be later events and none is held.","independent_command_check":"No clause has a different or independent duration. The restated Part D operates only as part of Executive Order No. 9871 as amended; item 2 supplies the shared sunset.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Allowances earned during the period before the sunset are payments for past service under the regulation; the held text creates no continuing duty after June 30, 1950, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the amended regulation.","scope_check":"Three operative pieces: the amending and extending lead, item 1 (Part D restated, including the meal-rate table and the quarters allowance proviso), and item 2 (effective date and continuation through the fiscal year). All three are tied to the same fiscal-year sunset, because the amended text of Executive Order No. 9871 and this order are said to continue in effect together."}
